instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Real estate developer specializing in urban residential projects including mid-rise apartment buildings and townhouse communities. Current pipeline of 350 units across 4 active projects. Evaluating modular construction methods and BIM-based cost estimation to reduce construction timelines. Enterprise-scale organization with complex multi-layer governance, dedicated innovation/R&D departments, and formal stage-gate project approval processes. We have substantial resources but also significant organizational inertia — aligning stakeholders across divisions takes deliberate effort and senior executive sponsorship.
answers.pastInitiatives: We experimented with a customer self-service portal two years ago after seeing competitors offer similar functionality. We built an MVP with an external agency in 3 months, but customer adoption was disappointing — only 8% of customers created accounts. We did not invest enough in understanding whether our specific customer base actually wanted self-service before building.
answers.strategicGoals: We operate in a consolidating market where competitors are merging to gain economies of scale. Our independent position is increasingly vulnerable. We need to proactively strengthen our competitive positioning — either by deepening our specialization in high-margin niches where scale matters less, or by building platform-like switching costs that make our offering stickier for existing customers.
answers.teamSize: Innovation is decentralized across business units, each with its own innovation lead and dedicated resources, coordinated by a group-level Chief Innovation Officer. The total innovation workforce is approximately 100 people across the organization. A group innovation fund of €5M annually is allocated competitively — business units pitch for funding against clear innovation KPIs including revenue from new products and process efficiency gains.
answers.additionalContext: We completed a merger with a similarly-sized competitor 4 months ago and are in the middle of integrating teams, systems, and processes. The combined organization has significant duplication — two CRMs, two HR systems, overlapping product lines. There is a unique window to redesign processes from scratch rather than patching legacy approaches, but cultural integration is fragile and change fatigue is real.

input.changes_since_last: Hired 5 new team members. Launched customer feedback pilot. Budget for innovation increased 25%.

opportunities.title: Post-Merger Digital Platform Unification and Experience Layering
opportunities.rationale: The merger presents a unique, time-sensitive window to redesign foundational processes (CRM, ERP) rather than patching legacy systems. A unified digital platform that creates high switching costs is critical for market defense in this consolidating sector. This requires deep organizational alignment.

first_actions: Establish a dedicated 'Integration Digital Task Force' with senior executive sponsors to mandate process harmonization across duplicated systems (CRM/HR).
Conduct rapid value mapping workshops involving end-users from both merged entities to identify core, non-negotiable functional requirements for the single source of truth.
Pilot a centralized data governance framework covering key customer interaction points identified during integration.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction of process duplication and identification of a single, unified customer journey map covering 80% of critical touchpoints.
milestones: Completion of To-Be State Process Map (Month 3)
Successful sandbox test integration of two core systems (CRM/ERP) (Month 6)

opportunities.title: Vertical Deep Specialization into High-Margin Niche Assets
opportunities.rationale: Given the difficulty and time investment required for broad platform building, Apex should pivot its market defense strategy. Identifying a highly specialized vertical (e.g., medical office parks or mixed-use sustainable rapid deployment) allows them to build deep expertise, creating specialization barriers rather than generic platforms.

first_actions: Form cross-functional 'Niche SWAT Teams' responsible for detailed market mapping and competitive analysis within 2-3 candidate high-margin verticals.
Develop a specialized product line focusing only on the efficiency gains or regulatory requirements unique to that niche, bypassing general offerings.
Pilot concept design with key industry advisory boards specific to the chosen niche.
execution_plan.success_metric: Development and successful pitch of a specialized product/service offering unique to the chosen niche vertical.
milestones: Final selection of target niche market (Month 3)
Creation of Minimum Viable Niche Offering (MVNO) concept (Month 6)

next_steps.action: Immediate governance review of the merger integration process to stabilize decision-making and allocate resources away from 'patching' legacy systems.
next_steps.owner: Chief Innovation Officer (CIO) / Executive Steering Committee

next_steps.action: Host cross-functional workshops to map the 'ideal' customer journey across all intended merged touchpoints, identifying single points of failure or data silos.
Re-evaluate the core assumptions behind the previous self-service portal failure by conducting qualitative interviews focused on 'why' customers didn't use it, rather than just 'if' they want it.

key_weaknesses: Significant organizational inertia and cultural friction resulting from the recent merger, hindering cross-functional cooperation.
Over-reliance on decentralized business unit funding/pitching models for core strategic initiatives, which slows necessary central process reform.
Process complexity due to duplication (two CRMs, two HR systems) creating systemic risk and inefficiency.

improvements: Increased innovation budget allocation by 25%, showing greater organizational commitment to digital transformation.
The launch of the customer feedback pilot indicates a shift toward formalized learning cycles beyond ad-hoc conversations.
Formal R&D structures and stage-gate processes are now in place, providing clearer governance for new initiatives.
persistent_gaps: Lack of centralized process ownership across merged entities, preventing the execution of radical unification projects.
Failure to translate market intelligence (e.g., competitor consolidation) into a singular, focused strategic pivot.
Maintaining change fatigue and stakeholder alignment during the critical merger integration phase.
achieved_milestones: Enhanced internal funding capacity for innovation projects.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The primary focus shifted from general exploration to critical post-merger operational unification and market defense strategy, providing clear windows for deep process redesign.
